examples.ko: 내일 오전에 팀장님께 중간보고를 해야 해요.
examples.en: I have to give the team leader an interim report tomorrow morning.
Have you finished making the materials for the interim report?
Many problems came up in the interim report.
The project's interim report is next Friday.

examples.ko: 중간보고는 짧게 핵심만 말하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: For an interim report, it's best to say only the key points briefly.
I haven't even given an interim report and the deadline is already here.

explain: 일이 끝나기 전에 진행 상황을 알리는 거라서 끝난 뒤의 '최종 보고'와 짝으로 써요. '중간보고를 하다'라고 하고, 윗사람에게는 '중간보고를 드리다'라고 해요. '중간 보고'처럼 띄어 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: I'll give an interim report on Friday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 진행 상황을 알리는 가장 기본 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to say you report on progress.

phrases.en: I gave an interim report to the team leader.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람에게 보고할 때 높여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific form for reporting to a superior.

phrases.en: After the interim report comes the final report.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 끝난 뒤의 보고로, '중간보고'와 짝이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The report after the work is finished; pairs with 중간보고.

explain_en: It reports progress before the work is done, so it pairs with '최종 보고' (final report). You say '중간보고를 하다', and '중간보고를 드리다' to a superior. It is sometimes written with a space as '중간 보고'.

en: to be sound; to be reliable

examples.ko: 그 회사는 규모는 작아도 경영이 견실해요.
examples.en: That company is small, but its management is sound.
It is safer to invest in a sound company.

examples.ko: 아버지는 견실하게 모은 돈으로 가게를 열었어요.
examples.en: My father opened a shop with money he saved steadily.

examples.ko: 저 친구는 생각이 견실해서 믿고 일을 맡길 수 있어요.
examples.en: That friend thinks in a reliable way, so I can trust him with work.

examples.ko: 이번 분기에도 견실한 성장을 이어 갔어요.
examples.en: It kept up its solid growth this quarter as well.

examples.ko: 견실하지 않은 계획에는 돈을 빌려주기 어려워요.
examples.en: It is hard to lend money for a plan that is not sound.

explain: 사람의 태도, 회사의 경영, 성장처럼 믿고 맡길 만큼 탄탄할 때 써요. 뉴스에서는 '견실한 기업', '견실한 성장'으로 자주 나오고, 반대말은 '부실하다'예요.

phrases.example: 회사가 견실한 성장을 이어 가고 있어요.
phrases.en: The company is continuing steady, sound growth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often seen in the news.

phrases.en: He does his assigned work reliably.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 태도가 믿음직할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person's attitude is dependable.

phrases.en: This company has solid finances.
phrases.nuance_ko: '견실하다'보다 쉽고 일상 대화에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 견실하다 and fits everyday talk.

explain_en: It describes a person's attitude, a company's management or growth as solid enough to rely on. In the news you often see '견실한 기업' and '견실한 성장', and the opposite is '부실하다'.

examples.en: The tax is paid automatically.
The tuition has not been paid yet.
When the fee is paid, they let you know by text message.

examples.ko: 기한 안에 납부된 금액은 돌려받을 수 없어요.
examples.en: The amount paid within the deadline cannot be refunded.
The insurance premium is paid from my salary every month.
I confirmed that the fine had been paid.

explain: 세금, 등록금, 보험료, 벌금처럼 기관에 내는 돈이 처리됐을 때 써요. 가게에서 물건값을 내는 것에는 쓰지 않고 '결제되다'를 써요. 내는 사람이 주어면 '납부하다'예요.

phrases.en: The amount that has been paid cannot be refunded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 기관에 낸 돈을 가리킬 때 쓰는 꾸밈말 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form for money already paid to an institution.

phrases.en: Please check whether the insurance premium has been paid.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이 처리됐는지 알아볼 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for checking whether a payment has gone through.

phrases.en: The tax must be paid within the deadline.
phrases.nuance_ko: 납부 기한이 중요한 세금이나 요금 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common when talking about taxes or fees where the payment deadline matters.

explain_en: Used when money owed to an institution, such as taxes, tuition, insurance, or fines, has been paid. For paying at a shop use 결제되다 instead. When the payer is the subject, it is 납부하다.

dis.h: paid to an authority: taxes, fees, bills
gh: payment processed, esp. by card or transaction
given out by the payer: wages, benefits
money handed over for goods or services

p.n: 납부 is paying what is due to an institution; 납입 is paying into an account in installments.

examples.en: The quality of this product is poor.
The machine stopped because of a defective part.
The factory picked out the faulty products.
I was scolded by the teacher for a bad attitude.
The weather was bad, so the plane took off late.

examples.ko: 성적이 불량하면 장학금을 받을 수 없어요.
examples.en: If your grades are poor, you cannot get a scholarship.

explain: 물건의 품질이나 사람의 태도가 나쁘다는 말이에요. '나쁘다'보다 딱딱하고 공식적이며, 상품과 부품에는 '불량품', '불량 부품'처럼 명사로 많이 써요. 학생이나 청소년에게는 '불량 학생'이라고 하지만 사람을 낮추는 말이라 조심해서 써야 해요.

phrases.example: 수업 시간에 불량한 태도를 보이면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You shouldn't show a bad attitude during class.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불량하다'를 사람의 태도에 쓰는 활용형이에요. 예의 없고 나쁜 태도를 딱딱하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form of '불량하다' used for a person's attitude, describing a rude or bad attitude in a formal tone.

phrases.en: The part is defective, so the machine keeps stopping.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말하는 연결형이에요. 물건의 품질이 나빠서 생긴 문제를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form that gives a reason, used to explain a problem caused by poor product quality.

phrases.en: This product's quality is not poor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불량하다'의 부정형으로, 품질에 문제가 없다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form of '불량하다', used to say there is no problem with the quality.

explain_en: It means something is poor in quality or a person's attitude is bad. It is stiffer than 나쁘다 and common with products as nouns: 불량품 (defective goods), 불량 부품. It can describe a student as 불량 학생 (delinquent), but that is a put-down, so use it carefully.

en: to be paid; to be disbursed

examples.en: The salary is paid on the 25th of every month.
The repair fee has already been paid.

examples.ko: 아직 돈이 지불되지 않아서 물건을 못 받았어요.
examples.en: The money hasn't been paid yet, so I couldn't get the item.
If you pay by card, it will be paid automatically.
The amount that has been paid cannot be refunded.
As soon as the deposit is paid, I'll give you the contract.

explain: 말할 때는 '내다'를 가장 많이 써서 '돈을 내다'라고 해요. '지불하다'는 조금 딱딱하고, '지불되다'는 계약서, 영수증, 공지 같은 글에 주로 나와요.

phrases.en: The fee was charged to my card.
phrases.nuance_ko: 카드나 앱으로 돈이 나갈 때 말할 때도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when money is taken by card or app. Also common in speech.
phrases.en_equiv: to be charged; to be settled

phrases.en: The meal cost has already been paid.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 벌써 냈다는 뜻이고, 안내문이나 영수증에 잘 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the money has already been paid. It shows up in notices and receipts.

phrases.en: The fee has not been paid yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이 아직 안 들어왔을 때 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used when payment hasn't been made yet.

explain_en: In speech people mostly say '돈을 내다'. '지불하다' is a bit formal, and '지불되다' appears mainly in contracts, receipts and notices.

dis.h: money handed over for goods or services
gh: payment processed, esp. by card or transaction
given out by the payer: wages, benefits
paid to an authority: taxes, fees, bills

p.n: 결제 sounds like a processed payment (card, account); 지불 is plain paying.

examples.ko: 짐 무게가 초과돼서 추가 요금을 냈어요.
examples.en: The baggage was overweight, so I paid an extra fee.
We must be careful not to go over budget.

examples.ko: 정원이 초과되어서 더 탈 수 없어요.
examples.en: The capacity has been exceeded, so no more can get on.
If the time limit is exceeded, points are deducted.

examples.ko: 한도가 초과된 카드는 쓸 수 없어요.
examples.en: A card that is over its limit cannot be used.

examples.ko: 인원이 초과될 것 같아서 일찍 신청했어요.
examples.en: The number of people looked likely to go over, so I applied early.

explain: 정해진 수나 양, 시간을 넘었을 때 써요. 반대말은 '미달되다'예요. '넘다'보다 딱딱해서 안내문과 규칙에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: If you go over the speed limit, you have to pay a fine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 주어일 때는 '초과하다'를 써요. '초과되다'는 수나 양이 주어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 초과하다 when a person is the subject; 초과되다 takes the amount as subject.

phrases.example: 인원이 열 명을 넘으면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: The number of people must not go over ten.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉽고 부드러운 일상어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler, softer everyday word.

phrases.en: This bus is over capacity.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문에서 자주 보는 명사 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun collocation often seen on notices.

explain_en: Use it when a set number, amount or time is passed. The opposite is '미달되다'. It is stiffer than '넘다' and often appears in notices and rules.

examples.ko: 태풍으로 인한 피해액이 수백억 원에 달해요.
examples.en: The damage from the typhoon amounts to tens of billions of won.
The government is investigating the exact amount of damage.

examples.ko: 이번 화재의 피해액은 아직 정확하지 않아요.
examples.en: The damage amount of this fire is not yet exact.
Will the insurance company compensate the amount of the loss?
The aid money differs depending on the amount of damage.
Compensation starts only after the damage assessment is done.

explain: 손해를 돈으로 계산한 금액을 말해서 뉴스, 보험, 재난 기사에 자주 나와요. '피해액이 달하다, 피해액을 산정하다, 피해액을 집계하다'처럼 짝으로 익혀 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: The damage from this flood is large.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피해 금액이 많다고 말할 때 쓰는 기본 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic way to say the amount of damage is large.

phrases.en: The insurance company investigates the amount of damage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손해가 얼마인지 알아볼 때 쓰는 말로 뉴스와 보험 이야기에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when finding out how much loss occurred; common in news and insurance talk.

phrases.en: The city hall is tallying the typhoon damage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 곳의 피해 금액을 모아 합친다는 느낌이 있는 공식적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal expression meaning to add up damage amounts from many places.

explain_en: It is the amount of loss counted in money, so it appears often in news, insurance and disaster reports. It is helpful to learn it in pairs like '피해액이 달하다', '피해액을 산정하다' and '피해액을 집계하다'.

examples.en: Airport staff quarantine the animals coming in.
The imported fruit was inspected first at the port.
How many days does it take to quarantine an animal?
The quarantine officer carefully inspected our luggage.

examples.ko: 수입 소고기를 검역한 뒤에 시장에 내놓아요.
examples.en: Imported beef is put on the market after it is inspected.

examples.ko: 입국장에서 사람들을 검역하지 않는 나라도 있어요.
examples.en: Some countries do not quarantine people at the arrival hall.

explain: 검역하는 쪽(검역관, 기관)이 주어일 때 쓰는 말이에요. 검역을 받는 입장에서는 '검역을 받다'라고 해요. 질병을 막는 일이라 '검사하다'보다 범위가 좁고 목적이 분명해요.

phrases.en: They thoroughly quarantine the livestock coming in at the airport.
phrases.nuance_ko: '철저히'를 붙이면 꼼꼼하게 확인한다는 느낌이 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '철저히' stresses careful checking.

phrases.en: All imported meat is quarantined.
phrases.nuance_ko: 검역을 받는 대상이 주어일 때 피동형을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form is used when the thing inspected is the subject.

phrases.example: 해외에서 온 식물은 먼저 검역해야 해요.
phrases.en: Plants from overseas must be quarantined first.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어야 하다'로 규칙이나 절차를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses '-아/어야 하다' to state a rule or procedure.

explain_en: This is used when the inspecting side, such as an officer or agency, is the subject. From the point of view of the one being checked, you say '검역을 받다'. Because it is about stopping disease, it is narrower and has a clearer purpose than '검사하다'.

examples.ko: 이 기관은 공신력이 높아서 사람들이 믿어요.
examples.en: This organization has high public credibility, so people trust it.

examples.ko: 정부 발표의 공신력이 떨어졌다는 말이 나와요.
examples.en: People are saying the credibility of government announcements has dropped.

examples.ko: 공신력 있는 자료를 찾아서 발표해야 해요.
examples.en: You should find reliable sources and present them.

examples.ko: 언론의 공신력은 한번 잃으면 되찾기 어려워요.
examples.en: Once the media loses its credibility, it is hard to regain.
It takes a long time to earn public credibility.

examples.ko: 그 제품은 공신력 있는 기관의 인증을 받았어요.
examples.en: That product received certification from a trusted institution.

explain: 사람 사이의 '믿음'보다 기관, 언론, 제도, 자료처럼 사회가 믿어 주는 대상에 써요. '공신력이 있다/높다/떨어지다', '공신력 있는 기관'처럼 자주 말해요. 친구를 믿는 이야기에는 '신뢰'나 '믿음'을 써요.

phrases.en: This newspaper has high public credibility.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사회가 많이 믿어 주는 기관이나 자료에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For institutions or sources that society trusts highly.

phrases.en: Look up data from a credible institution.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사를 붙여 믿을 만한 곳을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun to point to a trustworthy source.

phrases.en: Its credibility dropped because of a wrong announcement.
phrases.nuance_ko: 믿음이 줄어들었다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means public trust has declined.

explain_en: Rather than personal trust between people, it is used for things society trusts, such as institutions, the media, systems and sources. Common patterns are '공신력이 있다/높다/떨어지다' and '공신력 있는 기관'. For trusting a friend, use '신뢰' or '믿음'.

en: military service number; military serial number

examples.en: I received my service number when I enlisted.
He showed me the necklace with his service number on it.
My grandfather still remembers his service number.
Please write your name and service number on the form.
Once your service number is checked, you can go in.
What soldier doesn't even know his service number?

explain: 군인마다 따로 받는 번호로, 입대할 때 받아요. 학교에서 받는 '학번', 회사에서 받는 '사번'처럼 '번'이 붙는 말과 비슷해요. 군대 이야기를 할 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 군인은 자기 군번을 꼭 외워야 해요.
phrases.en: Soldiers must memorize their own service number.
phrases.nuance_ko: '군번'과 함께 쓰는 동사로, 번호를 기억해 둔다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A verb pairing with 군번, meaning to keep the number memorized.

phrases.en: Please write your name and service number on the form.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류나 명단에 군번을 쓸 때 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when writing the number on forms or lists.
phrases.en_equiv: to write down one's service number

phrases.en: First, state your name and service number.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대에서 자신을 소개할 때 둘을 함께 묶어 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The two are often paired when identifying oneself in the military.

explain_en: It is the number each soldier gets when enlisting. It is similar to other words ending in '번' such as '학번' (student number) and '사번' (employee number). It comes up often when people talk about the military.

examples.en: Customs seized hundreds of smuggled items.
There's a rumor that this watch is contraband.

examples.ko: 시장에서 밀수품을 사면 법을 어길 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you buy smuggled goods at the market, you could be breaking the law.

examples.ko: 밀수품은 값이 싸도 사지 않는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's best not to buy smuggled goods, even if they're cheap.
The enforcement team found a shop that sells contraband.

examples.ko: 압수한 밀수품 중에는 가짜 명품도 있어요.
examples.en: Among the seized contraband, there are also fake luxury goods.

explain: 세금을 내지 않고 몰래 들여온 물건이에요. 가짜 상품인 '짝퉁'과는 달라서, 밀수품은 진짜일 수도 있어요. 뉴스나 세관 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: A person who sold smuggled goods at the market was caught.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몰래 들여온 물건을 거래하는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when talking about trading in goods that were brought in illegally.

phrases.en: Customs stepped up its crackdown on smuggled goods.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a phrase often heard in the news.

phrases.en: Smuggled items are seized by customs.
phrases.nuance_ko: '밀수품'을 풀어서 말한 표현으로, 동사 '밀수하다'를 써서 더 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: This unpacks 밀수품 using the verb 밀수하다 and is easier to say.

explain_en: These are goods brought in secretly without paying duties. They differ from '짝퉁' (fakes), because smuggled goods can be genuine. The word often appears in news and customs stories.

examples.ko: 전 대통령의 서거에 많은 사람이 슬퍼했어요.
examples.en: Many people grieved at the passing of the former president.
A memorial service was held on the tenth anniversary of the passing.

examples.ko: 원로 시인의 서거로 문단 전체가 조용해졌어요.
examples.en: The whole literary world went quiet because of the passing of the senior poet.

examples.ko: 그분의 서거는 우리 모두에게 큰 슬픔이었어요.
examples.en: His passing was a great sorrow for all of us.
On the anniversary of his death, many citizens visit the grave site.

examples.ko: 서거를 알리는 뉴스를 보고 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: I cried when I saw the news announcing the death.

explain: 높은 분의 죽음을 말하는 아주 격식 있는 말이에요. 대통령이나 존경받는 어른처럼 사회에서 중요한 인물에게 뉴스에서 쓰고, 가족이나 친구의 일에는 '돌아가시다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 전 총리의 서거 소식이 전해지자 온 나라가 슬픔에 잠겼어요.
phrases.en: When news of the former prime minister's death spread, the whole country was plunged into grief.
phrases.nuance_ko: '서거'에 '소식'을 붙여, 뉴스에서 높은 분의 죽음을 알릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 소식 to 서거 is how the news reports the death of a highly respected figure.

phrases.example: 그 시인의 서거 1주기를 맞아 시집이 다시 나왔어요.
phrases.en: A new edition of the poetry collection came out for the first anniversary of the poet's death.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세상을 떠난 존경받는 인물의 첫 번째 기일을 격식 있게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal way to refer to the first anniversary of a respected person's death.

phrases.example: 많은 시민이 전 대통령의 서거를 애도했어요.
phrases.en: Many citizens mourned the former president's death.
phrases.nuance_ko: '서거'와 함께 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말로, 죽음을 슬퍼하며 추모한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation with 서거, meaning to grieve and pay respects over a death.

explain_en: This is a very formal word for the death of a respected figure. The news uses it for presidents or esteemed elders, but for family or friends people say '돌아가시다'.

examples.ko: 경찰이 사고 피해자의 신원을 확인하고 있어요.
examples.en: The police are confirming the identity of the accident victim.

examples.ko: 신원이 확실한 사람만 들어올 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only people whose identity is certain can enter.

examples.ko: 신원 조회가 끝날 때까지 기다려 주세요.
examples.en: Please wait until the identity check is finished.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 신원은 아직 밝혀지지 않았어요.
examples.en: That person's identity has not been revealed yet.
The company checks employees' backgrounds carefully.
You need one person to vouch for you.

explain: '이름'이나 '정체'와 달라요. 신원은 그 사람이 누구인지, 어떤 사람인지 증명되는 정보를 모두 말해요. 이름, 나이, 직업, 사는 곳 등이 들어가고, 뉴스에서 '신원을 확인하다', '신원 미상'처럼 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 입구에서 신원 확인을 한 다음에 들어갔어요.
phrases.en: I went in after my identity was checked at the entrance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신분증 같은 것으로 누구인지 확인하는 일에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for checking who someone is, for example with an ID card.

phrases.en: The accident victim is still unidentified.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누구인지 아직 모른다는 뜻으로 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it is not yet known who the person is, and it often appears in the news.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 끝까지 신원을 밝히지 않았어요.
phrases.en: That person never revealed who he was.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기가 누구인지 알려 줄 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for telling others who you are.

explain_en: Different from 이름 (name) or 정체 (true nature): 신원 covers the verified facts about who someone is, such as name, age, job and address. In the news you will often see 신원을 확인하다 (confirm the identity) and 신원 미상 (unidentified).

examples.en: The Nobel Peace Prize winner was announced.
He gave a speech after receiving the peace prize.
There is an organization nominated for the peace prize.
This year's peace prize went to a human rights activist.
I heard he donated the peace prize money to people in need.
Please explain the meaning of the peace prize.

explain: 대부분 '노벨 평화상'이라는 이름으로 뉴스에 나와요. '평화상을 받다', '평화상을 수상하다'처럼 쓰고, 받은 사람은 '평화상 수상자'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 그 활동가는 노벨 평화상 후보에 올랐어요.
phrases.en: That activist was nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize.
phrases.nuance_ko: '평화상'은 대부분 이 이름으로 뉴스에 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: '평화상' mostly appears in the news under this name.

phrases.en: This year a civic group won the peace prize.
phrases.nuance_ko: '받다'보다 격식 있는 말이라 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More formal than '받다', often used in news.

phrases.en: The peace prize winner visited Korea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상을 받은 사람을 가리키는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The pairing that names the person who won the prize.

explain_en: It mostly appears in the news as the '노벨 평화상' (Nobel Peace Prize). You say '평화상을 받다' or '평화상을 수상하다', and the recipient is the '평화상 수상자'.

en: to be built; to be constructed

examples.ko: 저 건물은 백 년 전에 건축됐어요.
examples.en: That building was built a hundred years ago.
A new library will be built here.
A hanok is a house built from wood.
It's a bridge built long ago, so it isn't sturdy.
A building is under construction, so it's noisy.

examples.ko: 그 성당은 오 년에 걸쳐 건축되었어요.
examples.en: That cathedral was built over five years.

explain: 집·성·다리 같은 큰 건물을 짓는 것에는 '건축하다'를, 일상 말에서는 '짓다'를 훨씬 많이 써요. 그래서 '집을 건축했어요'보다 '집을 지었어요'가 자연스러워요. '건축되다'는 건물의 역사나 설명글에 더 잘 나와요. 도로나 다리 공사는 '건설되다'도 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 이 집은 건축된 지 오십 년이 됐어요.
phrases.en: This house was built fifty years ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물의 나이를 말할 때 '~된 지 ~년'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '~된 지 ~년' to state a building's age.

phrases.en: A new building is under construction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 짓고 있는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a building is still being constructed.

phrases.en: My family built a house by the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '건축하다'보다 이 말을 훨씬 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is far more common than 건축하다 in everyday speech.

explain_en: For big structures like houses, castles and bridges, 건축하다 is the formal verb, but daily speech uses 짓다 far more: '집을 지었어요' sounds more natural than '집을 건축했어요'. 건축되다 shows up in explanations of a building's history. For roads and bridges, 건설되다 is also common.

dis.h: built as a house or building
gh: built as big works like roads or plants
created as land, a park, or complex

p.n: 건립되다 sounds more formal, like something founded.
